findings.fact: Ken Newquist describes sketching an original homegrown region, recreating it in Hexographer, then using Worldographer. Paper, digital map and notes diverged: a tower changed side, a town separation differed, and paper/digital hex offsets did not match. He reports reconciling the maps.
findings.interpretation: Primary evidence of both map creation and concrete maintenance friction. This is not a ready-made setting import, nor proof that an automatic generator alone solves the synchronization problem.

findings.fact: The same author identifies Scales of Truth as D&D5e, describes extending the map as play continues, updating it in Worldographer, and difficulty maintaining NPC/location journal entries after reconciliation. A subterranean mapping layer is a future plan.
findings.interpretation: Confirms edition-era and actual ongoing campaign context for the first article. Do not count the second post as another creator or a planned underground layer as completed work.
